questions.stem: What is the name of the theorem that states that the square of the hypotenuse is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two sides in a right-angled triangle?
questions.solution: The theorem that states the square of the hypotenuse is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two sides in a right-angled triangle is known as the Baudhayana-Pythagoras Theorem. This name reflects its historical roots in both Baudhayana's work and Pythagoras's later formulation. The other options are not recognized names for this mathematical principle.

questions.stem: In a right-angled triangle, which side is opposite the right angle?
questions.solution: In a right-angled triangle, the side opposite the right angle is called the hypotenuse because it is the longest side and connects the two legs. The base and perpendicular are the other two sides that form the right angle, and a vertex is a point where two sides meet, not a side itself.

hi.solution: एक समकोण त्रिभुज में, समकोण के विपरीत भुजा कर्ण कहलाती है क्योंकि यह सबसे लंबी भुजा होती है और दो पादों को जोड़ती है। आधार और लंब वे दो भुजाएं होती हैं जो समकोण बनाती हैं, और एक शीर्ष दो भुजाओं के मिलने वाले बिंदु को कहते हैं, भुजा नहीं।
